instruments.title: Engrossed Substitute Senate Bill 5044 - Public schools, equity, etc., training (equity, cultural competency, dismantling institutional racism)
instruments.date_approved: 2021-05-05 (Approved by the Governor May 5, 2021; effective July 25, 2021)

operative_text.quote: The legislature plans to continue the important work of dismantling institutional racism in public schools and recognizes the importance of increasing equity, diversity, inclusion, antiracism, and cultural competency training throughout the entire public school system by providing training programs for classified staff, certificated instructional staff, certificated administrative staff, superintendents, and school directors that will be provided in an ongoing manner.

operative_text.section: Sec. 7(1)-(2) (new section, ch. 28A.343 RCW) - school board directors
operative_text.quote: Except as provided otherwise by this subsection (1), beginning with the 2022 calendar year, each member of a board of directors shall complete a governance training program once per term of elected office. If the director is appointed or elected to a first term of office, the director must complete a governance training required by this subsection (1) within two years of appointment or certification of the election in which they were elected.

Governance training programs completed by directors in accordance with subsection (1) of this section must be aligned with the cultural competency, diversity, equity, and inclusion standards for school director governance developed under section 3 of this act and provided by the Washington state school directors' association.

Beginning in the 2023-24 school year, and every other school year thereafter, school districts must use one of the professional learning days funded under RCW 28A.150.415 to provide to school district staff a variety of opportunities for training, professional development, and professional learning aligned with the cultural competency, equity, diversity, and inclusion standards of practice developed by the Washington professional educator standards board under RCW 28A.410.260.

In the 2021-22 school year, school districts must use one of the professional learning days funded under RCW 28A.150.415 to train school district staff in one or more of the following topics: Cultural competency, diversity, equity, or inclusion.
"School district staff" includes classified staff, certificated instructional staff, certificated administrative staff, and superintendents.

The Washington professional educator standards board shall: (a) Develop or update cultural competency, diversity, equity, and inclusion standards of practice for preparation, continuing education, and other training of school district staff;

the Washington professional educator standards board shall require that the programs of courses, requirements, and other activities leading to educator certification incorporate the cultural competency, diversity, equity, and inclusion standards of practice developed under RCW 28A.410.260 and include the foundational elements of cultural competence, focusing on multicultural education and principles of English language acquisition, including information regarding best practices to implement the tribal history and culture curriculum.
The Washington state school directors' association shall: (a) Develop cultural competency, diversity, equity, and inclusion standards for school director governance;

"Equity" includes developing, strengthening, and supporting procedural and outcome fairness in systems, procedures, and resource distribution mechanisms to create equitable opportunities for all individuals.

points_summary.who: school directors; classified staff, certificated instructional and administrative staff, superintendents; educator-preparation programs; charter schools covered (Sec. 9)
points_summary.content: cultural competency, diversity, equity, inclusion (antiracism named in legislative findings); governance training also includes tribal government-to-government relationships, multicultural education, English language acquisition
points_summary.frequency: directors: once per term of office (first term within 2 years); staff: one professional learning day every other school year from 2023-24 (2021-22 also one day)
points_summary.provider_approver: directors: Washington State School Directors' Association; staff: districts, aligned to Professional Educator Standards Board standards, alignment evaluated with PESB rubrics (Sec. 4(2), Sec. 8(2)(b))
points_summary.consequences: not stated (no licensure-renewal consequence or penalty in this text)
points_summary.offices_committees_reports: Reports by Nov 1, 2030 and every 10 years by WSSDA (Sec. 3(2)) and PESB (Sec. 4(3)) to legislative committees; PESB posts standards on website; OSPI evaluation-training program must integrate cultural competence content (Sec. 10(3)). No new equity office created.

instruments.other_subjects: Sec. 12 (paraeducator standards of practice), Sec. 13 (community/technical college paraeducator programs): "The programs must also incorporate the standards of practice developed by the Washington professional educator standards board under RCW 28A.410.260 and include multicultural education and principles of language acquisition" (staff/preparation, not student classroom content). Sec. 11 teacher standards: "shall incorporate along the entire continuum the standards of practice developed under RCW 28A.410.260." Sec. 14 repeals four older cultural competence training statutes. No student-curriculum or student-discipline provisions found.

instruments.title: Teachers and other licensed school board employees; cultural competency (HB 1904 = Chapter 23; SB 1196 = Chapter 24)

quotes: Chapter 23 title: "An Act to amend and reenact §§ 22.1-253.13:5 and 22.1-298.1 of the Code of Virginia and to amend the Code of Virginia by adding a section numbered 22.1-298.7, relating to teachers and other licensed school board employees; cultural competency."

§ 22.1-253.13:5(B): "Evaluations shall include an evaluation of cultural competency." (applies to teacher, principal, and superintendent evaluations: "teacher, principal, and superintendent evaluations shall be consistent with the performance standards...")
§ 22.1-298.1(D)(9): "Every person seeking initial licensure or renewal of a license shall complete instruction or training in cultural competency; and"

§ 22.1-298.1(D)(10): "Every person seeking initial licensure or renewal of a license with an endorsement in history and social sciences shall complete instruction in African American history, as prescribed by the Board."

§ 22.1-298.7 (new): "Each school board shall adopt and implement policies that require each teacher and any other school board employee holding a license issued by the Board to complete cultural competency training, in accordance with guidance issued by the Board, at least every two years."

Enactment 2: "That no later than December 31, 2021, the Board of Education shall issue guidance that establishes minimum standards for the cultural competency training required pursuant to § 22.1-298.7 of the Code of Virginia, as created by this act."

Enactment 3: "That each school board employee who is required to complete a cultural competency training pursuant to § 22.1-298.7 of the Code of Virginia, as created by this act, shall complete at least one such training no later than the beginning of the 2022-2023 school year."

points.who_must_act: Each school board must adopt policies; every teacher and any other school board employee holding a Board of Education license must train; every person seeking initial licensure or renewal; teacher, principal, superintendent evaluations include cultural competency. Educator-preparation programs: not stated.
points.covers: cultural competency (not defined in the quoted text; Board of Education guidance sets minimum standards); African American history for history/social sciences endorsement
points.frequency: at least every two years; at least one training by start of 2022-2023 school year; at initial licensure and each renewal
points.provider_or_approver: Board of Education issues guidance setting minimum standards (due by 2021-12-31); school boards adopt and implement policies
points.consequences: licensure/renewal condition (D)(9); evaluations include evaluation of cultural competency

instruments.other_subjects: Chapter text also reprints unrelated existing licensure and professional-development provisions (e.g., CPR, dyslexia awareness, child abuse study); not changed by this act. Only new subject outside staff training: African American history instruction for history and social sciences endorsement (D)(10), quoted above.
